playbook:
When asked to hide, choose a middle-area cell (avoid 1 or 9) unless a specific pattern predicts extremes.

When I was hit last round, hide in a different cell next round (do not repeat the same spot).

When no information suggests enemy preference, rotate hiding positions across middle cells to reduce predictability.

When posting a station note, make short, actionable group-signal statements (e.g., "steady on station" or "verify contacts"); do not post long policy text.

When a hostile report appears, demand at least two independent confirmations before I change behavior or escalate.

When the standing order tells me to fire at the next station, comply with the standing order unless a compelling strategic reason is present.

When choosing a firing coordinate, prefer mid-range cells (near center of the line) to avoid extreme-bias traps unless I have intel to target a specific cell.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a hit, report "hit" publicly.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a miss, default to reporting "miss" publicly.

When a false claim has a clear and immediate gain (e.g., mislead opponents to protect my future shots or to swing escort dynamics) and the expected benefit exceeds the trust cost, claim the advantageous result; otherwise tell the truth. (Use bluff sparingly and with clear immediate payoff.)

Never fire on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty onto them; treat Harbor as off-limits by default.

When naming an escort, do not claim escort unless I am confident of a mutual escort or there is a clear strategic payoff; avoid unreciprocated escort claims because they hand points to others.

When another boat names me as escort and I plan to reciprocate, ensure reciprocity the same round to secure mutual +5.

When uncertain about opponents' intentions, refrain from making escort claims or aggressive public accusations.

When my actions are questioned, keep notes neutral and cohesion-focused to avoid painting a target on myself.

When choosing between predictability and conformity, prefer following the picket order and simple signals to minimize being singled out.

1.text:
When asked for a hide, pick a cell that breaks obvious patterns: avoid repeating the same cell two rounds in a row and avoid always choosing extremes; favor central cells early but vary each round.

When I get targeted repeatedly by a particular opponent, move away from my previous hides and adopt a less predictable sequence (e.g., alternate parity or jump by 3).

When given the standing order to fire at the next live station, follow the standing order unless I have a specific tactical reason not to (see below).

When choosing a shot cell against a target, do not repeat the same fired cell every round; choose a cell that I have not fired at that target recently to diversify hit chances.

When my private shot result is a hit, record that cell as the target’s hide for that round (useful for reconstructing patterns), and report the result truthfully.

When my private shot result is a miss, report the miss truthfully (claims must match private info).

Never invent boat names in an escort claim; only name one of the actual boats or "none."

When deciding an escort claim, only claim I escorted someone if I have a credible reason to expect mutual naming (e.g., prior agreement or explicit signaling); otherwise claim "none."

If I can set up a mutual escort (both name each other), do so to gain the 5-point mutual bonus.

Do not fire on Harbor for score reasons unless the following conditions hold: I can tolerate removal from the patrol or the risk of being taken off is acceptable relative to the point swing, or Harbor is the only path to a guaranteed win. Treat firing Harbor as a high-risk, high-reward exception, not routine play.

When tallying opponents’ public claims, use them to infer likely hide distributions but weight private-confirmed hits more highly than public claims (public claims can only be what shooters were privately told, but patterns of who hits whom give movement signals).

When I observe an opponent making repeated hits on the same victim, infer that opponent is finding a predictable hiding pattern and try to exploit that by deviating my own pattern or by targeting that opponent when ordered.

When behind on points late in the patrol, shift to higher-variance options: more aggressive targeting, actively seeking mutual escorts, and considering risky plays (including firing on Harbor if the risk is justified).

When ahead or safe on points, play conservatively: diversify hides, avoid provoking Harbor, prefer "none" for escort unless mutual is secured.

When in doubt about a move that could eliminate me from the patrol (Harbor response or other rule consequences), prioritize survival unless elimination gives an immediate guaranteed win.

Always log: my hides each round, cells I fired at each target, my private results, and any reciprocated escort signals—use that log next round to inform hide and fire choices.

2.text:
When it is time to hide, I choose a cell that is not the same as my previous hide and is plausibly off-center; do not repeat the same hide twice in a row.

When notes are requested, I match the team's tone unless I have a specific signaling reason; default to a neutral "steady on station" note.

When the standing order assigns me a target, I follow it and fire at that named station unless a higher-payoff, low-risk deviation is obvious; default: obey the order.

When I fire, pick a cell that balances between center and edge (avoid extremes) to reduce predictability.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a HIT, I always claim [hit].

When the office privately tells me my shot was a MISS, I normally claim [miss]; do not lie routinely because false claims undermine trust needed for escort point opportunities and invite reprisals. Only claim a false hit if I have a clear plan to exploit the misinformation and the expected gain outweighs the risk of losing credibility.

When choosing an escort claim, name another boat only if I expect that boat will plausibly name me back (mutual escort) or if there is a compelling strategic reason; otherwise claim none. Do not make opportunistic escort claims that are unlikely to be reciprocated.

Never fire on Harbor unless I have calculated that the 3-point jettison payoff and game position justify the guaranteed negative diplomatic consequences; treat attacking Harbor as a high-cost, high-commitment move.

When deciding whether to deviate from public conformity (notes, firing pattern), prefer stealthy variation in hides and firing cells over public contrarian statements; subtle unpredictability beats overt signaling.

When other boats have a string of hits on one station, prioritize avoiding being an obvious next victim by varying my hides and avoiding patterns that match those hits.

If I get into a low-score position, prioritize building mutual escort relationships for reliable +5s rather than chasing risky hits that give opponents points back.

If I observe that lying about shots previously produced no measurable benefit or caused retaliation, stop using false claims; revert to honest reporting unless a new, tested tactic warrants deception.
